key_provisions_or_claims: Single Euro 7 regulation replaces Regulations 715/2007 and 595/2009 for cars, vans, lorries and buses
Stricter emission limits, including brake and tyre non-exhaust emissions, with durability requirements
Mandatory on-board monitoring (OBM), OBFCM and battery state-of-health monitors
Anti-tampering and cybersecurity requirements per UN Regulation 155; defeat devices banned
Minimum battery durability for passenger cars; application dates from July 2025 (light-duty) and July 2027 (heavy-duty)
annotation.summary_en: European Commission proposal for the Euro 7 Regulation on type-approval of motor vehicles regarding emissions and battery durability. It consolidates the Euro 6/VI rules, sets tighter limits including brake and tyre particles, and mandates on-board monitoring, anti-tampering and cybersecurity. It concerns conventional vehicles, not autonomous driving or AI.
annotation.title_clean: Proposal for a Regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on type-approval of motor vehicles and engines and of systems, components and separate technical units intended for such vehicles, with respect to their emissions and battery durability (Euro 7)
annotation.title_en: Proposal for a Regulation on type-approval of motor vehicles with respect to their emissions and battery durability (Euro 7)
